reran: cmd.sh-equivalent on w4-int: exit 0, 11 'default4()' and 12 'scala.Double.box(2.0)' assertions at posterasure, class files written, program prints the right list. On w3-base and the 2.13.18 jars: fewer assertions plus NullPointerExceptions ('restpe is null'), exit 1 and no class files, so the hunter's claim holds. 2.13.11, 2.13.15 report it too; 2.13.10 and 2.12.20 are clean (no default label in that tree).
user_impact: Only compiler developers and plugin authors running -Ycheck:all (or -Ycheck:erasure and later), on any guarded literal switch whose arms are boxed (result Any with primitive arms). On 2.13.18 the check also aborts compilation of such code. The generated bytecode is correct.
fixability: clear cut: in SwitchMaker (MatchOptimization.scala, wrapInDefaultLabelDef) give defaultLabel the type the match is checked against (pt, as the matchEnd label has) rather than b1.tpe.deconst, falling back to the body type when pt is not fully defined. No compatibility cost; check that the backend's switch emission still recognises the shape.
regression: in 2.13.11 (first release where this tree carries a default label; the commit was not identified)
links: X2 / retronym/scala#419 and #459 (non-destructive -Ycheck): why w4-int writes class files and the base does not. H4, H11, H60, Z19 (retronym/scala#460, #509): other -Ycheck reports, different causes. WP2, WP4: sibling -Ycheck findings from the same harness.
note: Not a checker false positive, and the hunter's mechanism is wrong. The tree is inconsistent: patmat types the default label from its body (default4 gets info ()Double from 2.0), erasure then boxes the body and types the LabelDef and its jumps as Object while the label symbol's info stays ()Double. The checker retypes from the symbol and finds Object where Double is declared. Refutation of 'label defined in a later case is not pre-entered': the same shape with String arms (no boxing) and with result Double (no boxing) checks clean; the report needs boxing. Any later phase or plugin that reads the label symbol's result type after erasure sees the wrong one.
